answer: A stake-weighted work queue resists Sybils: claiming a task needs a bond slashed if the output fails verification, and seats go by committed capital, not by how many wallets someone can create. A thousand empty identities win nothing, since collateral is locked per seat and cannot be cloned across fakes. Each attempt burns compute and time, so attack cost scales with capital at risk plus idle opportunity cost. To capture even a small share an attacker needs a gale of liquidity exposed to slashing, while an atlas of past slashes and a clear opal-like audit trail make ghost identities costly.
